messages:
Sophie R: seeing a tail latency cliff starting ~08:12 UTC on shared-gpu pool us-west-2c, affects a handful of long-context tenants. Grafana: https://graf.redwood/g/abc123/longseq-tail (spikes ~3x P95->P99).
Ash M: noticed kernel-autoswitch events around that time in the kernel-audit logs. Might be flipping from tiled_fast to fused_v2 for certain seq lengths.
Kevin L: pulled perf profiles, here's the flamegraph link: https://perf.redwood/fg/3175 and a short nvprof heatmap: https://nv.redwood/hm/3175. Kernel selectors are switching at batch_size ~6 / seq ~8192.
Maria G: KV cache eviction rate also jumps at the same time. I see hotset churn: kv_hits drops from 0.88 -> 0.62. Might be combined effect: kernel flip increases memory working set and forces KV evict, causing more recompute.
Tom S: operator note: autoscaler bumped pool from 12->18 gpus at 08:15 but that didn't help tail. Probably orthogonal.
Sophie R: snippet from runtime logs around the event:
```
[08:12:06] kernel_selector: selected tiled_fast for model-x (seq=2048, batch=3)
[08:12:07] kernel_selector: swapped -> fused_v2 reason=throughput_hint
[08:12:07] kv_cache: eviction_count=1245
[08:12:07] kernel_runtime: out_of_slots=false mem_pressure=0.72
```
Kevin L: interesting that mem_pressure isn't maxed. Suggests fused_v2 increases transient allocations (scratch) which cause KV fragmentation. pprof shows frequent small allocs in attention_kernels.
Maria G: reproducer on my staging: run a mixed workload (many short chats + occasional long history eval). When kernel autoswitch allowed, we see kv eviction wave and 200-500ms tail spikes for long requests. When forcing kernel pinned to tiled_fast the tail goes down.
Sophie R: can we do emergency mitigation? options I see: 1) pin kernel for affected tenants 2) raise per-tenant kv_quota 3) temporary rate limit/rlimit for noisy tenant 4) disable autoswitch in shared pool until fix.
Ash M: +1 for pinning per-tenant kernel as lowest risk. We can add an override at routing layer to set kernel_hint for tenant id.
Kevin L: I pushed a small canary patch that allows per-tenant kernel_hint: repo/runtime#issue-1220. Config example:
```
route_overrides:
  tenant: t1234
  kernel_hint: tiled_fast
```
I'll deploy to canary pool now.
deploy-bot: deploy started: runtime/canary/patch-1220 -> pool-usw2c-canary by Kevin L
infra-bot: canary provisioned: 3 gpus in pool-usw2c-canary (labels: shared-longseq-testing)
Maria G: ran a 2-hour synthetic mix against the canary. Results: P99 tail for long requests dropped from 980ms -> 420ms, kv_eviction_rate reduced ~60%. Proms: https://graf.redwood/g/abc123/canary-3175
Tom S: rolled a short-term routing rule to divert top noisy tenants to canary with kernel_hint pinned. Applied at 08:50.
Sophie R: great. Who owns the long-term fix? I think kernel selection heuristic needs to consider transient scratch allocation and KV working set estimate. Also need to add per-tenant soft KV quotas and a better eviction policy (LRU by tenant-hotness).
Ash M: i'll take kernel selector changes (heuristic tuning + adding a predictive model that uses seq distribution + historical kv footprint). Plan: prototype + perf run next week. Owner: Ash M.
Kevin L: i'll own KV quota and eviction policy improvements (per-tenant quotas, decaying hotness score). Will propose design doc by EOD Thu. Owner: Kevin L.
Maria G: I'll work on an observability dashboard to detect these correlated switches earlier: kernel_switches vs kv_evictions vs tail_latency. Add an alert runbook.
Sophie R: temporary actions summarized: (A) pin kernel_hint for affected tenants (done for canary) (B) route noisy tenants to canary / dedicated pool (done) (C) monitor canary and prepare rollback trigger if anything breaks (ops).
Tom S: created follow-up ticket runtime/1221 to track rollout and test matrix.
Sophie R: risk note: pinning avoids autoswitch benefits for some other workloads; need to be surgical. We'll only pin tenants with >P99 impact >300ms and >kv_eviction threshold.
Kevin L: suggestion for intermediate improvement: change autoswitch threshold to require both throughput and mem-scratch delta >X for Y seconds, reduces flapping.
Ash M: agreed. I'll add hysteresis and a min-stable-window param.
Sophie R: ok let's sync tomorrow 09:30 PT, invite eng-runtime + eng-ml. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
